relationships.subject: Oxypeucedanin
relationships.evidence_quote: CCI surgery resulted in a significant increase in the LPA content and the expression level of LPAR1 in the mouse spinal cord, which could be completely reversed by OPD treatment (Figures 5B–5D).

relationships.subject: Oxypeucedanin
relationships.evidence_quote: CCI surgery increased the protein expression level of RhoA, which was attenuated by OPD (40 mg/kg) treatment.

relationships.subject: LPAR1
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that genetic over-expression LPAR1 could activate the downstream RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway and induce neuropathic pain-like phenotype in mice

relationships.subject: Oxypeucedanin
relationships.evidence_quote: Daily treatment with OPD at three dose levels (10–40 mg/kg) all maintained the anti-allodynic effects without producing the trend of analgesic tolerance in SNI mice (Figure 3B).

relationships.subject: Y-27632
relationships.evidence_quote: daily treatment with CCG-1423 (20 mg/kg, i.p.) or Y-27632 (30 mg/kg, i.p.) significantly attenuated CCI-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, similar to the effect of OPD

key_findings: Oxypeucedanin relieves neuropathic pain in mice by inhibiting spinal LPAR1/RhoA/ROCK signaling.
LPAR1 overexpression reverses OPD antinociception while LPAR1 silencing mimics it.
